If the MYPLUGIN_API macro and module dependencies are correctly configured but the LNK2019 persists—especially after a rename or move—the issue is likely a desynchronization between the Unreal Header Tool (UHT) and the linker’s memory.

Live Coding & Hot Reload Limitations

According to the official Live Coding Primer and Unreal Header Tool documentation, these systems have specific structural limitations regarding the reflection system:

  • Header Changes: Live Coding is primarily intended for logic changes within .cpp files. Changes to headers that modify UCLASS, UFUNCTION, USTRUCT, or UENUM are not fully supported for hot-patching.
  • Symbol Re-exporting: When you rename a class or a UFUNCTION, UHT generates new reflection symbols (like Z_Construct_...). Live Coding cannot always re-bind these new symbols to the existing linker memory of the running editor, leading to “unresolved external symbol” errors during the patch process.
  • Stale Objects: The documentation notes that while “Object Reinstancing” is enabled by default to help objects take on structural changes, lingering instances of the old class name or old function signatures can cause conflicts in the destructor or reflection registry, often resulting in crashes or linker failures.

The Recommended Clean Workflow (The “Nuclear Option”)

When UHT becomes stale or Live Coding fails to resolve generated symbols after a structural change (like a rename), Epic recommends a full manual regeneration. This process clears the “stale” .gen.cpp files located in the Intermediate folder.

Step-by-Step Clean Process:

  1. Shutdown: Close the Unreal Editor and your IDE (Visual Studio/Rider). Ensure the LiveCodingConsole.exe is also closed.
  2. Delete Cache Folders: In your project root AND your Plugin folder, delete the following directories:
    • Binaries/ (Contains the compiled DLLs that Live Coding tries to patch).
    • Intermediate/ (Contains the stale MyWidget.gen.cpp and UHT manifest files).
    • DerivedDataCache/ (Optional, but recommended for structural changes).
  3. Regenerate Project Files: Right-click your .uproject file and select Generate Visual Studio project files. This forces Unreal Build Tool (UBT) to re-scan the headers and create a fresh manifest for UHT.
  4. Cold Rebuild: Open the .sln file and perform a Rebuild (not just a Build) on your project. This ensures UHT runs from scratch, generating the correct Z_Construct symbols for the new class name.

Best Practices to Prevent Reoccurrence

  • Disable Live Coding for Structural Changes: If you plan to rename classes, add new UFUNCTION entries, or change UPROPERTY specifiers, turn off Live Coding, make the changes, and restart the editor with a fresh compile.
  • Avoid Hot Reload: For C++ plugins, Live Coding (Ctrl+Alt+F11) is the preferred iteration method over the legacy “Hot Reload” (the Compile button in the editor), but neither is a substitute for a cold start when the UHT metadata changes significantly.
  • Check FailIfGeneratedCodeChanges: In the Unreal Header Tool documentation, it is noted that UHT uses a -FailIfGeneratedCodeChanges flag during hot reloads to prevent exactly this type of linker corruption. If you see this error, it is a signal that a full restart is required to synchronize the generated reflection code.

Documentation References:

  • Live Coding Primer: Section on “Common Issues” regarding header file changes and data structures.
  • Unreal Header Tool Overview: Section on the two-phase compilation process and UBT/UHT synchronization.
  • FAQ: C++ Programming: Guidance on when to use cold compiles versus Live Coding.
